szoveg_eredeti:
O’FALLON, Mo. (InvestigateTV) — Artificial intelligence is on the frontlines of fighting crime and being used in may 911 dispatch centers around the country.

The police dispatch in O’Fallon is using artificial intelligence-based technology to assist dispatchers who answer 911 calls. Dispatchers there said a person will always answer the call.

Based on the call, the technology displays a specific list of questions for the dispatcher to ask. It also listens in, transcribes the call in real time and suggests information the dispatcher might have missed.

Paul Jokerst, emergency communications administrator for O’Fallon Police, said the technology is there to assist dispatchers.

“It is clearly here to assist. It’s just to assist them,” Jokerst said.

He said the technology is not intended to replace dispatchers.

“It’s not here to replace anybody. It’s not here to take a job away or hamper somebody’s job,” Jokerst said.

O’Fallon police dispatcher Mike Conte said he supports the use of AI.

Conte said the technology helps when dispatchers are trying to pick out information they cannot understand from a caller.

“It’s very helpful when we’re trying to pick out pieces of information that we can’t understand the caller,” Conte said.

He said he supports the technology as long as he is also on the line.

“You will always talk to a human. One of us is always here. And we’re always ready to answer your call,” Conte said.

The use of AI in 911 is expanding rapidly.

In Fairfax, Virginia, AI translates calls into more than 170 languages instantly.

In New Orleans, AI automatically answers calls about accidents officials already know about. The system will inform the caller about the incident and if they are involved in any way the person can stay on line to talk to a dispatcher.

Experts say AI would not replace dispatchers at the moment because humans are better at compassion, processing emotion and keeping people calm.

AI in law enforcement continues to evolve.
